messages.subject: Reason for missing abundance values
parts:
Hello MSstats team,
I am analyzing a dataset and I noticed that for some missing intensities, there is "predicted" abundance, and for others is not. 
I wanted to ask under which condition the "predicted" abundance is generated? Which command stands for this prediction and what are the parameters I have control over?
I'm attaching the data process code I used and an example of the "missing" predicted abundance I'm talking about.

Thank you!

(In the picture: three of the marked rows have no intensities, but the prediction was made only for the third one and not the upper two)

dataProcess(
  raw,
  logTrans = 2,
  normalization = "equalizeMedians",
  nameStandards = NULL,
  featureSubset = "all",
  remove_uninformative_feature_outlier = FALSE,
  min_feature_count = 0,
  n_top_feature = 10,
  summaryMethod = "TMP",
  censoredInt = "NA",
  MBimpute = TRUE,
  remove50missing = FALSE,
  fix_missing = NULL,
  maxQuantileforCensored = 1,
  use_log_file = TRUE,
  append = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
)

messages.author: 5c6e92c10ef28984
messages.subject: Re: Reason for missing abundance values
parts:
Hi,
as a first check, please try re-running after removing the option maxQuantileforCensored = 1 (to keep it at default value).
Kind regards,
Mateusz
